arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Walter Dellinger argued the Amendment responded to fears about federal control of state militias.
Paul Clement argued the text guarantees an individual right independent of militia service.
Chief Justice Roberts noted that acknowledging an individual right shifts the focus to the reasonableness of regulations.

paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the Second Amendment. One side argues it protects individual self-defense. The other side argues it protects only organized militia service.

paragraphs: The government wants the Court to uphold the local ban on handgun possession.
The individual wants the Court to strike down the local ban on handgun possession.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues the Amendment protects only the right to serve in a state militia.
The individual argues the Amendment protects a personal right to keep firearms for self-defense.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Chief Justice Roberts asked why the text says the right of the people if it only applies to militias.
Justice Scalia asked how a personal guarantee and a militia assurance can coexist without contradiction.
